subject: Tier mapping & marketplace fee impact — hosted API per-token discounts
messages:
From: Evan Myers <evan.myers@acmeco.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing: marketplace fee / commit tier mapping

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking my call this morning. Procurement at Acme wants two things clarified before we can proceed to a PO:

1) How do Redwood's per-token volume discounts layer with marketplace billing? We purchase through GCP Marketplace and need to understand the visible unit price vs. the net Redwood revenue after marketplace fees.
2) For committed tiers (monthly and annual), what does a pass-through to our invoicing look like? Do you quote gross (our invoice includes the marketplace fee) or net (Redwood absorbs marketplace fee and we get the same discount)?

Attached is a short note from our procurement team with constraints — they require a marketplace line item where possible. Can you send a sample tier mapping (per-token price at X/100M tokens, X/500M tokens, X/1B tokens) showing both direct billing and marketplace billing columns?

Would prefer a spreadsheet we can attach to our internal approval packet.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Myers
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Co.
Evan.Myers@acmeco.com
Attachment: Acme_PO_Constraints.pdf (pdf, 112KB)

From: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Myers <evan.myers@acmeco.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: marketplace fee / commit tier mapping

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. I pulled together an initial tier mapping and attached an editable spreadsheet (Redwood_Tier_Mapping_v1.xlsx). A few quick clarifications before we send a formal quote: 

- Marketplace fee visibility: marketplaces (GCP/AWS/Azure) levy a partner/transaction fee that is collected by the marketplace. Typically that fee is between 10–15% depending on the marketplace and listing. Our standard practice is to quote the gross list price and call out the marketplace fee as a separate line so your finance team can see the pass-through.
- Net revenue vs customer-visible price: If you require the net (Redwood) price to match our direct invoice pricing, we can either: (A) offer a reduced list price to offset the marketplace fee (requires a marketplace-specific addendum / resale pricing), or (B) provide a committed rebate at year-end to net to the same economics. Each has procurement/legal tradeoffs.
- Commit tiers: in the spreadsheet I included three commitment bands and two billing models (monthly commit and annual prepay). Please confirm target monthly tokens so we can tune the breakpoints.

I'll loop in Karthik (pricing) and Aditya (billing/finance) to propose the two clean quoting paths that will pass procurement sign-off.

Notes attached: Redwood_Tier_Mapping_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 36KB)

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Evan Myers <evan.myers@acmeco.com>

Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acmeco.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: marketplace fee / commit tier mapping

Olga,

Thanks — quick answers from our side so you can re-run the numbers:
- Target steady-state: ~200M tokens/month first year, with bursts up to 600M in Q4.
- Procurement constraint: must use GCP Marketplace for invoicing (they will not accept direct vendor invoices for this purchase).
- Preferred outcome: pricing that appears on our Marketplace invoice; acceptable to show a separate marketplace surcharge line.

CFO wants to see a comparison table that shows:
A) List price + marketplace surcharge + final invoice amount
B) Implied net Redwood revenue per token (what Redwood would actually receive after marketplace fees)

I can share CFO contact for final approval if needed.

Lydia from Procurement is cc'd — she handles the PO and timing.

Evan
Attachment: Acme_PO_Constraints.pdf (resend)

From: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Myers <evan.myers@acmeco.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: marketplace fee / commit tier mapping

Evan / Lydia — appreciate the volume guidance and the procurement requirement. We ran two clean quoting workflows and attached an updated spreadsheet (Redwood_Tier_Mapping_v2.xlsx) plus a short note on how marketplace fees are shown (Marketplace_Fee_Impact.pdf). High level recommendation: 

Option 1 — Marketplace invoice (preferred for your procurement):
- We publish a GCP Marketplace listing with the list unit price (per 1K tokens) and the marketplace will add its fee as a visible surcharge line on your invoice.
- To preserve target net economics for Acme, Redwood can offer an adjusted list price for marketplace listings so that after the marketplace fee your net-per-token to Redwood approximates the direct billing net. This requires a marketplace-specific pricing entry (we've done this before) and a short reseller addendum for the contract.

Pros: clean procurement flow, appears on your Marketplace invoice, faster PO acceptance.
Cons: requires one-time marketplace listing adjustment and legal addendum; timeline ~7–10 business days.

Option 2 — Direct vendor quote with rebate: 
- Redwood issues a direct quote with committed tiers and invoice directly. You'd pay Redwood and maintain internal reconciliation with GCP.
- We can offer a committed rebate to bridge the marketplace fee if you prefer the invoice to reflect the same economics.

Pros: simpler for Redwood legal; faster to contract on our side.
Cons: Procurement at Acme may not accept direct invoices.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Please confirm you want us to prepare a marketplace-specific listing (Option 1). If so, we will: (a) create adjusted list prices for each tier (in Redwood_Tier_Mapping_v2.xlsx), (b) prepare a short addendum for marketplace resale pricing, and (c) provide a DocuSign quote link for signature.
2) If you prefer Option 2, confirm and we will prepare a direct quote + rebate schedule.

I copied Karthik and Aditya to confirm tax / accounting and Neha for commercial approval on the adjusted list. Karthik / Aditya / Neha — anything to add on implementation timing and accounting for marketplace pass-throughs?

—Olga
